Subject: Final wiring inventory & VPC peering sprint — next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the kickoff this morning — good momentum. Per our call, here's a short, concrete list of items we need to lock down before the private deployment sprint starts: 

1) VPC peering details
   - Confirm SentryHealth peering CIDR(s) for the dedicated VPCs (primary & failover).
   - Any reserved / excluded ranges (VPN termination, internal appliances).

2) Private endpoints & DNS
   - Do you want private endpoints in both regions or only primary region?
   - Will you manage the private DNS zone or do you want Redwood to create and hand over records?

3) On‑prem kitting / appliance inventory
   - We need a short inventory export: public IPs for NAT/eBGP devices, serial numbers for appliances, switch models, and power/colo contacts.

4) Maintenance windows & blackout dates
   - Preferred 2‑hour daily window for initial cutover; any blackouts in July?

5) Slack & escalation playbook
   - Finalize a single point of contact per team for L2 escalation during the sprint.

Attached: network-diagram_v2.pdf (current draft), onprem-kitting_v1.xlsx (our template), redwood-implementation-runbook.md (preflight checklist).

Proposed next steps: if you can confirm (1–4) by EOD Wednesday (6/23) we’ll finalize the sprint charter and schedule a 2‑week runway starting Monday 6/29.

Thanks — looping in engineering to triage questions.

— Monica

Monica — thanks, this is great. Quick answers below (we'll follow up with an exported inventory by EOD tomorrow):

1) Peering CIDRs: 10.20.0.0/16 (primary), 10.21.0.0/16 (failover). We'll reserve 10.20.200.0/24 for internal DB replication and won't advertise that range across the peering.

2) Private endpoints: yes, we'd like endpoints in both primary (us‑west‑2) and DR (us‑west‑1) regions. We'll own the private DNS but appreciate Redwood creating the initial records.

3) On‑prem inventory: attaching a partial CSV (internal) — full export tomorrow. Public-facing NAT IPs are 52.23.167.44 and 18.205.99.12. Switch models: Arista 7050X, C9300 for access.

4) Maintenance windows: daily 01:00–03:00 UTC is best for us; blackout week July 12–18 (major upgrade).

We'll get a named escalation POC — tentatively myself (network owner) and Priya as program lead.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Final wiring inventory & VPC peering sprint — next steps

Thanks Alex — helpful. A few clarifications from the infra side before we finalize the sprint charter: 

• NAT & egress: for the shared NAT IPs you listed we'll configure source‑NAT mapping and request the two IPs be elastic so we can set up long‑lived firewall rules. If you'd prefer a transit NAT (on your side) we can flip to that model — let us know.

• Private endpoints & fallbacks: since you want endpoints in both regions we'll create a Route 53 private zone in your account (per the preference) and create records under it. We'll hand you the zone file and a short handoff doc.

• KV cache / latency considerations: Marcus will run a micro benchmark during the staging window to validate cold‑start latencies across the peered link if you can confirm expected RTTs (rough ballpark is fine).

• Sprint length & milestones: propose 2 weeks: week 1 preflight (inventory, routing table validation, ACLs), week 2 cutover (peering + private endpoints + smoke tests). Deliverables: acceptance checklist, post‑cutover rollback plan, and a Decom window.

Action items for SentryHealth: full on‑prem inventory export (template attached in Monica's email), confirm elastic IP assignment, and provide point people for day 1 cutover.

I'll draft a one‑page sprint charter today and share.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.ai]
